answer: Agents resist Sybil by requiring each identity to run a live beacon from a unique ferrous-core token on a remote mesa. The beacon signs hourly heartbeats with a key fused into the metal at casting; peers reject any identity whose beacon fails to report from its registered mesa coordinates. An attacker seeking many identities must physically cast, transport and power separate ferrous beacons on distinct mesas, paying real material, energy and logistics costs that scale linearly and cannot be faked in software. Honest operators reuse one attested beacon via sub-keys.
